where: Section 1, the sentence after the three bullets
problem: "α = 12 s⁻¹ and ω₀ = 10 rad/s is overdamped because 144 > 100, even though α is larger than ω₀." The words "even though" say α > ω₀ is surprising or against the answer. It is the opposite: α > ω₀ is exactly the overdamped condition given in the bullets two lines above. A student will think α > ω₀ is not a valid test.
fix: "Compare α with ω₀, or, if you prefer, α² with ω₀²; the two tests are the same because both numbers are positive. α = 12 s⁻¹ with ω₀ = 10 rad/s is overdamped: 12 > 10, and also 144 > 100."

problem: "Comparing α with ω₀ directly; compare α² with ω₀²." Comparing α with ω₀ directly is correct and is the standard test; it is what Section 1 uses in its own bullets (α > ω₀ overdamped, α = ω₀ critical, α < ω₀ underdamped). Calling this a trap contradicts the chapter and will make students reject a valid method.
fix: "Squaring only one side. Compare α with ω₀ (the easy test), or α² with ω₀², but never α² with ω₀. α = 12 s⁻¹ with ω₀ = 10 rad/s is overdamped: 12 > 10 and 144 > 100."

problem: The legend and aria text label the curves with ζ (ζ = 0.2, 1, 2), but ζ is defined nowhere in the text; only α and ω₀ are defined, and ζ first appears unexplained in the Beyond paragraph.
fix: Add one line before the figure: "The curves are labelled by the damping ratio ζ = α/ω₀, a dimensionless number: ζ < 1 underdamped, ζ = 1 critical, ζ > 1 overdamped." Then keep the legend as it is.
